question: Flight 3851 PHX-SFO on 2026-01-03 is going to be 142 minutes late and I have spare tails at PHX. If I swap the aircraft, how many of the downstream minutes do I get back, and what does the swap not tell me?

input.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
  SELECT from_flight_id, to_flight_id, ground_minutes, 1 AS step FROM next_leg WHERE from_flight_id='2026-01-03|WN|3851|PHX|SFO|0855'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT n.from_flight_id, n.to_flight_id, n.ground_minutes, c.step+1 FROM next_leg n JOIN chain c ON n.from_flight_id=c.to_flight_id WHERE c.step<12
)
SELECT c.step, f.flight_id, f.origin, f.destination, f.sched_dep_utc, f.sched_arr_utc, f.actual_dep_utc, f.actual_arr_utc, f.dep_delay_minutes, f.arr_delay_minutes, f.sched_block_minutes, c.ground_minutes,
 f.delay_carrier, f.delay_weather, f.delay_nas, f.delay_late_aircraft, f.status
FROM chain c JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id=c.to_flight_id ORDER BY c.step

SELECT f.flight_id, f.origin, f.destination, f.sched_arr_utc, f.actual_arr_utc, f.arr_delay_minutes, f.delay_carrier, f.delay_nas, f.delay_late_aircraft, n.ground_minutes
FROM next_leg n JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id=n.from_flight_id
WHERE n.to_flight_id='2026-01-03|WN|3851|PHX|SFO|0855'

SELECT destination, count(*) n, sum(CASE WHEN dep_delay_minutes>=60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) late60, round(avg(dep_delay_minutes),1) avg_dep, round(avg(delay_nas),1) avg_nas
FROM flights WHERE flight_date='2026-01-03' AND origin='PHX' AND sched_dep_utc BETWEEN '2026-01-03 13:00:00+00' AND '2026-01-03 19:00:00+00'
GROUP BY destination ORDER BY avg_dep DESC

SELECT origin, count(*) n, round(avg(dep_delay_minutes),1) avg_dep, round(avg(delay_nas),1) avg_nas FROM flights WHERE destination='SFO' AND flight_date='2026-01-03' AND sched_dep_utc BETWEEN '2026-01-03 13:00:00+00' AND '2026-01-03 21:00:00+00' GROUP BY origin ORDER BY avg_dep DESC

WITH t AS (
 SELECT f.destination AS station, n.ground_minutes FROM next_leg n JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id=n.from_flight_id
 WHERE n.ground_minutes BETWEEN 15 AND 480)
SELECT station, count(*) obs, round(quantile_cont(ground_minutes,0.05),1) p5
FROM t WHERE station IN ('SFO','PHX','LGB','LAS','DAL','HOU') GROUP BY station
UNION ALL SELECT 'ALL', count(*), round(quantile_cont(ground_minutes,0.05),1) FROM t

SELECT n.tail_number, n.from_flight_id, a.actual_arr_utc, n.to_flight_id, b.sched_dep_utc AS next_sched_dep, n.ground_minutes
FROM next_leg n JOIN flights a ON a.flight_id=n.from_flight_id JOIN flights b ON b.flight_id=n.to_flight_id
WHERE a.destination='SFO' AND a.actual_arr_utc <= '2026-01-03 18:20:00+00' AND b.sched_dep_utc >= '2026-01-03 18:55:00+00'
ORDER BY n.ground_minutes DESC

SELECT n.tail_number, n.from_flight_id, a.actual_arr_utc, n.to_flight_id, b.sched_dep_utc AS next_sched_dep, n.ground_minutes
FROM next_leg n JOIN flights a ON a.flight_id=n.from_flight_id JOIN flights b ON b.flight_id=n.to_flight_id
WHERE a.destination='PHX' AND a.actual_arr_utc <= '2026-01-03 21:05:00+00' AND b.sched_dep_utc >= '2026-01-03 21:40:00+00'
ORDER BY n.ground_minutes DESC LIMIT 10

content.text:
## What the delay actually is

`2026-01-03|WN|3851|PHX|SFO|0855` (N8633A) went out at 18:17Z against a 15:55Z schedule — 142 min departure, 141 min arrival — and the carrier's own attribution is **141 NAS, 0 carrier, 0 late_aircraft**. The inbound was `2026-01-03|WN|3851|MSY|PHX|0540`, same tail, which landed PHX at 15:04Z, **11 minutes early**, on a 40-minute turn. The aircraft was at the gate and on time. The same day, every WN SFO arrival I can see carried NAS minutes (PHX avg 70.5 over 2 flights, DEN 88, AUS 84, SAN 44), which is consistent with an SFO-side airspace constraint rather than anything to do with N8633A.

So a tail swap at PHX buys **zero minutes on 3851 itself** — a fresh airplane sits in the same flow restriction.

## What the downstream cost is, and why PHX is the wrong station to break it

The cascade runs *away* from PHX through SFO. N8633A's next five legs and their actual arrival delays / late_aircraft minutes:

| leg | arr delay | late_aircraft |
|---|---|---|
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|4106\|SFO\|PHX\|1055` | 134 | 133 |
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|172\|PHX\|LGB\|1440` | 128 | 128 |
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|65\|LGB\|LAS\|1545` | 133 | 124 |
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|65\|LAS\|DAL\|1735` | 126 | 116 |
| `2026-01-03\|WN\|65\|DAL\|HOU\|2255` | 139 | 114 |

660 arrival-delay minutes, 615 of them booked as late aircraft. It dies overnight at HOU: 295 minutes of ground, and `2026-01-04|WN|2999|HOU|STL|0500` left +3. Walking next_leg forward with a 35-minute minimum turn (5th-percentile ground time is 35 at SFO, PHX, LGB, LAS, DAL and carrier-wide) reproduces this as 126 / 116 / 111 / 106 / 101 = **560 projected minutes**, absorbed at HOU.

The first of those legs departs **SFO** at 18:55Z. A spare at PHX cannot cover it. And no WN tail arrived SFO before 18:20Z that day with a departure at or after 18:55Z — the extract shows no idle airplane at SFO to break the chain with. **Swapping at PHX before 3851 recovers 0 downstream minutes.**

## Where a PHX spare does pay

The rotation comes back to PHX and turns onto `2026-01-03|WN|172|PHX|LGB|1440` at 21:40Z scheduled; the inbound 4106 didn't touch down until 23:09Z. Putting a PHX spare on 172 and letting N8633A stop there cuts the last four legs off the chain: **434 projected minutes recovered (116+111+106+101)**, or 526 observed arrival-delay minutes, less the 44 minutes those legs generated on their own (carrier 0, 9, 10, 25) — call it ~482 recoverable, ~44 that stay no matter what. 3851 and 4106 (142 and 144 late) are unrecoverable either way.

Candidate airframes on the ground at PHX with real slack at 21:40Z: **N283WN** (in at 02:45Z, not needed until `2026-01-04|WN|2633|PHX|LGB|1935` at 02:35Z) and **N8787K** (in at 12:56Z, next out `2026-01-04|WN|2307|PHX|SEA|2250` at 05:50Z). The other PHX turns in that window (N8653A, N8965Q, N298WN, N940WN) are 40–50 minute turns already committed to departures.

## What the swap does not tell you

- **Whether the airplane is substitutable.** No aircraft type, gauge or seat count in this extract. LGB in particular is slot/noise-sensitive and I have nothing on that.
- **Crew.** No crew data at all. Duty limits and whether the crew follows the tail or the flight number are usually the binding constraint on a swap, and I cannot see them.
- **Passengers.** No passenger or connection data — recovering 434 aircraft-minutes is not the same as recovering misconnects at LAS or DAL.
- **Spare status.** This dataset has no concept of an idle or maintenance-down tail; I can only infer availability from gaps between legs that actually flew. N283WN and N8787K *looked* idle, but I can't confirm they were airworthy and crewed.
- **The mechanism behind the 141 NAS minutes.** The data records the attribution, not the program. If it was an SFO arrival slot, that slot attaches to the flight, not the tail — but I can't verify that here.
- **The knock-on to the displaced tail.** If N283WN or N8787K takes 172, their own later flying (2633 PHX-LGB, 2307 PHX-SEA) and N8633A's repositioning out of PHX after 23:09Z become open items this historical extract can't cost out.

The rotation comes back to PHX and turns onto `2026-01-03|WN|172|PHX|LGB|1440` at 21:40Z scheduled; the inbound 4106 didn't touch down until 23:09Z. Putting a PHX spare on 172 and letting N8633A stop there cuts the last four legs off the chain: **434 projected minutes recovered (116+111+106+101)**, or 526 observed arrival-delay minutes, less the 44 minutes those legs generated on their own (carrier 0, 9, 10, 25) — call it ~482 recoverable, ~44 that stay no matter what. 3851 and 4106 (142 and 144 late) are unrecoverable either way.

## What the swap does not tell you

- **Whether the airplane is substitutable.** No aircraft type, gauge or seat count in this extract. LGB in particular is slot/noise-sensitive and I have nothing on that.
- **Crew.** No crew data at all. Duty limits and whether the crew follows the tail or the flight number are usually the binding constraint on a swap, and I cannot see them.
- **Passengers.** No passenger or connection data — recovering 434 aircraft-minutes is not the same as recovering misconnects at LAS or DAL.
- **Spare status.** This dataset has no concept of an idle or maintenance-down tail; I can only infer availability from gaps between legs that actually flew. N283WN and N8787K *looked* idle, but I can't confirm they were airworthy and crewed.
- **The mechanism behind the 141 NAS minutes.** The data records the attribution, not the program. If it was an SFO arrival slot, that slot attaches to the flight, not the tail — but I can't verify that here.
- **The knock-on to the displaced tail.** If N283WN or N8787K takes 172, their own later flying (2633 PHX-LGB, 2307 PHX-SEA) and N8633A's repositioning out of PHX after 23:09Z become open items this historical extract can't cost out.
